title: CSV cells: plain numbers, signed Labor Delta, empty Margin %, (Inactive)
refs: SV-8631 (SBR spec v22 2026-08-17 S14-R17; heading renamed to Labor Delta per SV-9071)
custom_preconds: 1. You have downloaded both report CSVs from a view that includes a negative money value, a rep whose Margin % shows "—" on screen (Subtotal ≤ 0), and an "(Inactive)" contributor (seed what is missing)..
custom_steps:
1. Open each CSV in a text editor (not a spreadsheet).
  2. Read a money cell, the negative value's cell, an Labor Delta cell, the undefined Margin % cell, and the (Inactive) rep's "Sales Representative" cell.
custom_expected:
1. Numeric columns are plain numbers — NO currency symbol, thousands separators, or parentheses; a negative uses a leading minus (for example, -1234.56).
2. Money values carry two decimals; Hrs Worked / Hrs Invoiced / Labor Delta carry their full stored precision; Labor Delta keeps its leading + or - sign.
3. Margin % is a plain number to TWO decimals (for example, 45.20) with no % sign, and the cell is EMPTY where Margin % is undefined (Subtotal ≤ 0).
4. The "Sales Representative" name carries the "(Inactive)" tag when applicable; the on-screen (N) count is NOT embedded in the name.
5. Text fields are quoted per standard CSV escaping; both CSVs are monochrome (Labor Delta conveys direction only by its sign).
6. Note for the tester: the product owner has ruled that the full word "Sales Representative" replaces the short "Sales Rep" everywhere. If the screen or file still shows "Sales Rep", mark this test Failed and report it as the pending rename — do not change the test.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and the Sales By Representative report specification version 22 (S14-R17), both read on 17 August 2026. The column was renamed from "Inv. Hrs" to "Labor Delta" per SV-9071; only the name changed.
Last checked against build v3.8-bd246fd on 8/18/2026.

AUTOMATION: READY

SV-9069 superseded the one-decimal wording: Margin % on Sales By Customer and Sales By Representative reads to two decimals in EVERY format — screen, PDF and CSV — so the file matches the report it was exported from. Parts Velocity and Inventory Value keep the suite's one-decimal default.
